*Reasoning as the farmer:*

Aiyo, me and this land, we've been together 50 years now. My two boys work in town — factory jobs, better money than farming — so most days it's just me and the old lady on these 16.9 mu. Son comes back for the busy weeks, wheat harvest and maize planting, otherwise I hire the combine and the seeder. At my age, I'm not about to be pulling a plow.

I do wheat-maize like everyone in the village. Always have. The land is decent — not the best, not the worst. I remember three years back we had a dry autumn and my neighbor old Wang planted too early, his wheat came up weak. I waited a week and mine was fine. So I watch the weather, I don't rush.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant around October 10-15, depending on soil moisture. I use the "Jimai 22" variety — the seed shop sells it, most of us grow it, good enough. Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (二铵 type, 15-15-15 or thereabouts) — that's my base. Then at green-up in March I topdress about 15 kg urea. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll add another 10 kg, but usually I don't need to. Works out to maybe 18 kg N per mu total. I water it 3-4 times: once before winter if dry, then green-up, jointing, grain-fill. Well water is metered now, costs real money, so I don't waste it. I spray herbicide once in spring for the broadleaf weeds. Yield — I usually get around 450 kg/mu, some years better, some worse.

**Maize (summer):** As soon as wheat comes off in early June, I get the no-till planter in — no time to plow, the village cooperative has one we share. "Zhengdan 958" or similar hybrid, whatever the shop has that year. I put 30 kg compound at planting and maybe 15 kg urea at big flare stage. Sometimes I skip the topdress if rain has been good. Irrigation depends — if July-August rains come proper, I don't water at all. If it's dry I'll water once or twice. Herbicide after emergence, and I watch for corn borer. Yield is usually 500 kg/mu or so.

I'm careful with money. My boys send some back but I don't want to be a burden. Fertilizer prices went up again this year, I heard, so I won't be putting extra on. What worked last year will work this year.
